Hi Tessa —

Thanks for sending the MSA. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed and attached a marked-up PDF (Helios_MSA_markedup.pdf). We've got a few asks on the insurance sections before we can sign the order form:

- Can you confirm you will accept a retroactive date for Cyber/Technology E&O that is 24 months prior to the service start (rather than a blanket inception date)?
- We need confirmation that Additional Insured (AI) is limited to obligations arising under the Order Form only (we can't accept blanket AI across all contracts).
- Our broker is flagging a sublimit carve-out for PCI/CC data investigations — is Redwood able to accept a $250k sublimit for cardholder data breach response?
- Will Redwood accept a waiver of subrogation limited to physical property loss only (no blanket WoS for all carriers)?
- Finally, can you provide a sample COI naming HeliosCloud and the language you expect on primary/non-contributory? Our broker prefers an insurer letter if primary/non-contrib is required.

If you want to route to your legal team, please cc them. We're hoping to close the order form by next week if these can be resolved quickly.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Questions on insurance sections in MSA redlines

Tessa / Marcus —

Thanks for the ping and the Helios redlines. I reviewed the annotated MSA and here are our proposed positions and rationale (intended to be compromise language that should close the request quickly):

1) Retroactive date (Cyber/E&O): Acceptable as limited relief. We can agree to a retroactive date equal to 24 months prior to the service start date, provided Helios confirms there are no ongoing or threatened claims predating that retroactive date. Proposed clause: "For Technology Errors & Omissions coverage, Insured's retroactive date shall be no later than twenty-four (24) months prior to the Service Start Date."

2) Additional Insured (AI): We will agree to AI but strictly limited to liabilities arising from Redwood's performance under the specific Order Form(s). Proposed clause to include "solely to liabilities arising out of Redwood's performance thereunder" and capped to the OF term. No blanket AI across other agreements.

3) PCI sublimit carve-out: We will accept a dedicated sublimit for cardholder data breach response in the amount of $250,000 provided the policy evidences such sublimit and the carrier confirms scope. This must be reflected on the COI or insurer letter. Note: acceptance is conditional on seeing insurer documentation from the broker confirming the sublimit.

4) Waiver of Subrogation (WoS): We will accept WoS but limited to physical property loss only. We cannot agree to a general WoS across all policies.

5) Primary / Non-Contributory: We prefer an insurer letter (carrier confirmation) when policy wording can't be captured on a COI. If Helios' broker can provide a standard carrier letter confirming primary and non-contributory status with the carrier's signature, that satisfies our requirement.

Next steps:
- Marcus: confirm with the broker if the insurer can produce a carrier letter and whether the $250k PCI sublimit can be shown on the policy schedule.
- Tessa: if Marcus confirms, prepare an updated Order Form that incorporates the AI/retro language and references the COI + carrier letter as fulfillment evidence.

I can provide tracked redline language for the MSA/OF if helpful — attaching a short snippet I plan to propose (helios_coi_draft.pdf).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachment: helios_coi_draft.pdf (proposed clause snippets)
